title: Self-duality of rho section modules at characteristic-dependent weights
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure] and $S$ a semisimple simply connected $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme], with semisimple and simply connected defined as in [lem-sfb-rho-section-modules]. Fix a split maximal torus $T\subseteq S$ and a Borel subgroup $B\supseteq T$, and use the character $\rho$, its extension $\widetilde\rho:B\to\mathbf G_m$, and the actual regular-function modules $W_m\subseteq F[S]$ of [lem-sfb-rho-section-modules]. A rational $S$-module is an $F$-vector space $V$ with a coaction $\rho_V:V\to V\otimes_F F[S]$ satisfying the coassociativity and counit identities; $V^S=\{v:\rho_V(v)=v\otimes1\}$. Tensor products have diagonal coaction. All equivariance and invariance below mean identities of coactions, equivalently identities after every commutative $F$-algebra extension. Write $W_m^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_F(W_m,F)$ with contragredient action $(s\ell)(w)=\ell(s^{-1}w)$ after every scalar extension. If $\operatorname{char}F=0$, then for every $m\ge1$ there is an equivariant linear isomorphism $W_m\simeq W_m^\vee$. If $\operatorname{char}F=p>0$, then for every integer $\nu\ge1$ and $m=p^\nu-1$ there is an equivariant linear isomorphism $W_m\simeq W_m^\vee$. No self-duality is asserted for general $m$ in positive characteristic.

source.place: Lemma 9.7.4(1),(2), Seshadri Property II, p.247; Alper printed pp.49--50. Apply to the constant group over R=F[[t]] and reduce the equivariant isomorphism modulo t. Local PDF WANTED; HTML https://arxiv.org/html/1005.2398v3#S9.SS7 read.

proof.text: Fix $m\ge1$. By [lem-sfb-rho-section-modules], $W=W_m$ is nonzero finite-dimensional rational. Set $\chi=-m\widetilde\rho$; the defining equations give $W=E_B(\chi)$, with identical left action. By [lem-sfb-induced-module-primitive-line], $W^U$ is a line of weight $w_0\chi$. Since $w_0\Phi^+=-\Phi^+$, in the rational character lattice $w_0\rho=\frac12\sum_{\alpha>0}w_0\alpha=-\rho$; this is a lattice calculation, valid also in characteristic $2$. Thus $W^U$ has weight $m\rho$.

source.place: 22.21--22.22, Theorems 22.18--22.19, discussion following 22.31, and Proposition 22.41; Steinberg irreducibility from Jantzen II.3.18--3.19 (local source WANTED). Assembly for Alper Lemma 9.7.4, field case.

proof.text: If $\operatorname{char}F=0$, [lem-sfb-characteristic-zero-complete-reducibility] writes $W=\bigoplus_{i=1}^a V_i$ with $V_i$ simple. Each $V_i^U$ is a line by [lem-sfb-simple-module-dual-highest-weight]. Fixed vectors in a finite direct sum are componentwise fixed, so $W^U=\bigoplus_i V_i^U$. Step 1 gives $a=1$, and $W$ is simple for every $m\ge1$.

proof.text: In either case $W$ is simple, and Step 1 identifies its highest weight as $m\rho$. By [lem-sfb-simple-module-dual-highest-weight], $W^\vee$ is simple with highest weight $-w_0(m\rho)=m\rho$. The same cited theorem gives an equivariant linear isomorphism $W\simeq W^\vee$. This is an isomorphism of rational coactions and therefore has the required equivariance after every scalar extension.

Step 1: W_m = E_B(-m rho~), since W_m has f(gb)=rho~(b)^m f(g) and E_B(lambda) has lambda(b)^{-1}, matching Milne (142). primitive-line then gives a U-fixed line of weight w0 chi = m rho. Step 2 (char 0): Milne 22.41 complete reducibility, plus dim V_i^U = 1, plus componentwise fixed vectors, gives one summand, so W is simple. Step 3 (char p): the Steinberg node with r = nu is literally W_{p^nu-1}. In Jantzen's convention (negative Borel) this is H^0((p^r-1)rho) = St_r. Step 4: Milne p.471 gives lambda(V^vee) = -w0 lambda(V) = m rho, and Milne 22.31 says simple modules with the same highest weight are isomorphic, so W is isomorphic to its dual. All three new nodes are true, self-contained, statement-only and not restatements of the item. Small cases tested: S=1, SL2, p=2, nu=2.
